reductionDefinition: Reduction from Exact Hitting Set to Exact Cover by transposing which elements belong to which subsets. Karp (1972, p. 99) gives the same transpose in the other direction, from Exact Cover to Hitting Set.
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
complexity: O(subSets * universalSet), sizes of HITTINGSET's own sets

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Exact Hitting Set = {<U, S> | U is a set, S is a family of subsets {S_i} of U, and there is a set W subset of U such that, for each i, |W intersect S_i| = 1}.
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: Exact Hitting Set is the problem of finding a set W of elements of U that shares exactly one element with each subset S_i. This is the Hitting Set of Karp (1972, problem 15). It is stricter than the Hitting Set of most later texts, such as Garey and Johnson (SP8), which only requires W to share at least one element with each subset and to have at most k elements.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: U, a universal set, and S, a collection of subsets of U
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether a set W exists that shares exactly one element with each subset in S
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {(U,S) | U is set, S subset {a | a subset U}} Example: ({1,2,3,4},{{1,3},{2,3,4},{1,4}})
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: W subset U | W intersects every subset in S in exactly one element Example: {1,2}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Exact Hitting Set. It tests every subset of U and returns the first one that intersects every subset in S in exactly one element.

timeComplexity.Description: , n = |universalSet|, s = number of subsets in S

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Exact Hitting Set. It checks that W is a subset of U and that W intersects every subset in S in exactly one element.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Exact Hitting Set

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Exact Hitting Set. It tests every subset of U and returns the first one that intersects every subset in S in exactly one element.

timeComplexity.Description: , n = |universalSet|, s = number of subsets in S

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Exact Cover = {<S, X> | S is a collection of subsets of a set X where S* exists such that S* is a subcollection of S and an exact cover, of S. This means that each element of X is in exactly one subset of S*.}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: The exact cover problem is a decision problem to determine if an exact cover exists for some <S, X>
reductionTo.inputDescription: X, a set, and S, a collection of subsets of X
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether an exact cover of X exists using subsets from S
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {T | T subset S, union of T = X, T pairwise disjoint} Example: {{1,4},{3,5,6},{2,7}}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a generic brute force solver for Exact Cover

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Exact Cover

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Exact Cover
